summary: Henderson Field is a remote military-civilian airport situated on Sand Island within Midway Atoll, one of the northwesternmost Hawaiian Islands and part of the United States Minor Outlying Islands. The airfield takes its name from Major Lofton R. Henderson, a U.S. Marine Corps aviator killed during the Battle of Midway in June 1942, and the original runway was constructed by the Navy during World War II. Today it primarily supports the Midway Atoll National Wildlife Refuge and is one of the most isolated airfields in the world.
faqs:
Q: Can I fly to Henderson Field as a regular passenger?
A: No, there are no scheduled commercial flights. Access is restricted to U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service personnel, researchers, contractors, and occasional charter operations.

Q: What is the runway situation at Henderson Field?
A: The airport has a single asphalt runway (designated 06/24) approximately 7,800 feet long, capable of handling large military and cargo aircraft including C-17s and C-130s.

Q: Is Henderson Field open to the public?
A: General public access is not permitted. Visitors must obtain special permission from the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service well in advance and arrange charter or government transport.

Q: How far is Henderson Field from the nearest major airport?
A: It is extremely remote, with Honolulu International Airport being roughly 1,300 miles to the southeast across open Pacific Ocean.
transport_tips: There are no taxis, buses, or rental cars on Sand Island; visitors typically arrive via chartered or military flights and are met by refuge staff for transport to the small number of on-island accommodations. Travelers should arrange ground transportation with their sponsoring organization before arrival since on-island services are extremely limited. Be prepared to walk between buildings as the small community is compact and pedestrian-friendly.
local_tip: Pack your own supplies including snacks, medications, and any specialty items — the island has no stores or shops, and resupply shipments are infrequent, so once you're there, what you brought is essentially all you have access to.
